name: OpenResearcher-30B-A3B

lineage.how_derived: SFT on 96K long-horizon trajectories (100+ turns) distilled from GPT-OSS-120B with its native browser tools

purpose: Agentic LLM for long-horizon deep research, fine-tuned by TIGER-AI-Lab and collaborators to show a fully open pipeline for synthesizing deep-research trajectories (arXiv 2603.20278) with an offline retrieval corpus instead of paid search APIs.

license.name: MIT (card tag) on a base under the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License
license.notes: No MIT text found: the HF repo has no LICENSE file and the GitHub repo LICENSE path returned 404. The base model's license text was read (https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/agreements/enterprise-software/nvidia-nemotron-open-model-license/, summarizer): 'Works are commercially usable', 'You are free to create and distribute Derivative Works', redistribution with a copy of the license, a Notice file 'Licensed by NVIDIA Corporation under the NVIDIA Nemotron Model License' if the work ships a NOTICE, license ends if you sue over infringement by the Work; no guardrail clause. Training data distilled from GPT-OSS-120B (Apache-2.0). Commercial use is therefore allowed under both texts, but the MIT claim itself is unverified.

architecture.why_this_design: Not an architecture contribution: the model is the Nemotron 3 Nano hybrid (nemotron_h) base. The paper's stated design choice is the data pipeline: trajectories are synthesized offline over a 15M-document corpus with three browser primitives (search, open, find) so that 97K+ long trajectories can be produced without live search API cost.

other: vLLM (vendor script scripts/start_nemotron_servers.sh, OpenAI-compatible endpoint on port 8001)
engine_support.notes: Tool requirements (repo README, summarizer; paper abstract): the model was trained on gpt-oss 'native browser tools' with three primitives search, open and find, and the client runs with use_native_tools=True against an OpenAI-compatible server. Search backend is selected by browser_backend: 'local' (self-hosted BM25 or dense retrieval service, needs no key, used for BrowseComp-Plus) or 'serper' (Serper Google Search API, needs SERPER_API_KEY, used for BrowseComp, GAIA and xbench). OPENAI_API_KEY is needed only for scoring. Context window and turn limit are not stated; training trajectories have 100+ turns. A user found the Serper free credits gone in about 2 minutes and asked how to stay fully local.

user_reports.summary: First impressions: install smooth but incomplete instructions; the demo burnt the free Serper credits in about two minutes, which defeats running local AI; the user asks how to avoid the Serper dependency (browser_backend local needs its own retrieval service).

tona_fit.reason: Only research-agent model with an official GGUF, vendor BrowseComp-Plus 54.8 percent above Tongyi DeepResearch on the same benchmark, a fully local retrieval option, license permissive in practice (NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License text read, MIT claim unverified). Needs a browser-tool harness (search, open, find) and a search backend. Missing nemotron_h_moe coverage is only a blocker.
blockers: browser-tool harness and a search backend
